key_responsibilities: Develop/maintain software on Jetson and Rockchip edge devices
Integrate and troubleshoot cameras, sensors, networking, peripherals
Build device services (capture, health monitoring, telemetry, config, remote mgmt)
Diagnose across Linux, device software, networking, power, hardware
Support bring-up and validation of new edge hardware
Deploy and evaluate ML models on edge
Travel to customer sites for installs and debugging

llm_analysis.reasoning: The core of this role (Jetson edge software, TensorRT model deployment, camera/sensor integration, and debugging at the hardware-software boundary) maps almost one-to-one onto Justin's COFFIN capstone and Object Tracking Turret. The real distance is production/field maturity, not skills: everything Justin has built is single-device lab/prototype scope, while this job is about fleets of devices running in customer warehouses.
strengths: Jetson + TensorRT + YOLO edge deployment (COFFIN: 5.2x TensorRT speedup, real multi-camera capture pipeline)
Hardware-software boundary debugging (COFFIN: resolved servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, false-positive detections; Turret: Jetson->STM32 over UART)
Camera/sensor integration (multi-camera multiprocessing capture; ADXL345, VL53L0X ToF, I2C sensors)
Python + C++ across the whole stack (CUDA C++, bare-metal C)
Practical hardware: PCB fab in EAGLE, oscilloscope/logic-analyzer bring-up, UART/I2C/SPI wiring
real_gaps: Zero production fleet experience: no OTA updates, device provisioning, fleet management, or cloud telemetry
No real-world/field customer deployment (all work is lab/academic)
No Rockchip/RK3588, no camera-interface protocols (MIPI CSI, GMSL, GigE, V4L2), no video pipeline tooling (GStreamer/RTSP), no Docker
Field electrical troubleshooting (tracing warehouse wiring, replacing components, multimeter work) is lighter than the resume's PCB/bench work implies
overstated_by_keywords: Linux debugging (has Linux usage, not deep systemd-services/networking-stack debugging)
electrical troubleshooting (bench/PCB depth, not field diagnostic depth)
